## File: vfs/memory/resolver.go
````go
package memory

import (
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
	"strings"

	"wails-app/internal/pathref"
	internalplatform "wails-app/internal/platform"
)

type PathResolver struct {
	store          *Store
	configuredRoot func() string
}

func NewPathResolver(appName string, configuredRoot func() string) (*PathResolver, error) {
	store, err := NewStore(appName)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := internalplatform.EnsureHiddenPath(store.RootPath()); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &PathResolver{store: store, configuredRoot: configuredRoot}, nil
}

func normalizeRoot(path string) string {
	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(path)
	if trimmed == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(trimmed))
}

func pathKey(path string) string {
	cleaned := filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(strings.TrimSpace(path)))
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
		cleaned = strings.ToLower(cleaned)
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(cleaned, `\\/`)
}

func (r *PathResolver) currentRoot() string {
	if r.configuredRoot != nil {
		if root := normalizeRoot(r.configuredRoot()); root != "" {
			return root
		}
	}
	return filepath.Clean(r.store.DataPath())
}

func (r *PathResolver) joinUnderRoot(root string, child string) string {
	if child == "" {
		return filepath.Clean(root)
	}
	return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(child)))
}

func (r *PathResolver) containsPath(root string, candidate string) bool {
	rootKey := pathKey(root)
	candidateKey := pathKey(candidate)
	if candidateKey == rootKey {
		return true
	}
	sep := string(filepath.Separator)
	return strings.HasPrefix(candidateKey, rootKey+sep)
}

func (r *PathResolver) relativeToRoot(root string, target string) (string, bool) {
	rootKey := pathKey(root)
	targetKey := pathKey(target)
	if targetKey == rootKey {
		return "", true
	}
	sep := string(filepath.Separator)
	if !strings.HasPrefix(targetKey, rootKey+sep) {
		return "", false
	}
	rel := strings.TrimPrefix(filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(target)), filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(root)))
	rel = strings.TrimLeft(rel, `\\/`)
	return filepath.ToSlash(rel), true
}

func (r *PathResolver) ResolvePublicPath(path string) (string, bool, error) {
	normalized := pathref.Normalize(path)
	if !pathref.IsMemory(normalized) {
		return normalized, false, nil
	}

	root := r.currentRoot()
	rest := strings.TrimPrefix(normalized, pathref.MemoryScheme)
	if rest == "" {
		return filepath.ToSlash(root), true, nil
	}

	target := r.joinUnderRoot(root, strings.TrimPrefix(rest, "/"))
	if !r.containsPath(root, target) {
		return "", true, fmt.Errorf("memory path escapes configured root")
	}
	return filepath.ToSlash(target), true, nil
}

func (r *PathResolver) ToPublicPath(path string) string {
	root := r.currentRoot()
	target := filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(path))
	rel, ok := r.relativeToRoot(root, target)
	if !ok {
		return filepath.ToSlash(path)
	}
	if rel == "" {
		return pathref.MemoryScheme
	}
	return pathref.MemoryScheme + filepath.ToSlash(rel)
}

func (r *PathResolver) BackingRoot() string {
	return filepath.ToSlash(r.currentRoot())
}
````

````go
package memory

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

type Store struct {
	rootPath  string
	statePath string
	dataPath  string
}

func NewStore(appName string) (*Store, error) {
	base, err := os.UserConfigDir()
	if err != nil {
		base, err = os.UserHomeDir()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	dir := filepath.Join(base, appName, "memoryfs")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, "data"), 0755); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	return &Store{
		rootPath:  dir,
		statePath: filepath.Join(dir, "state.json"),
		dataPath:  filepath.Join(dir, "data"),
	}, nil
}

func (s *Store) ReadState() ([]byte, error) {
	return os.ReadFile(s.statePath)
}

func (s *Store) WriteState(data []byte) error {
	return os.WriteFile(s.statePath, data, 0644)
}

func (s *Store) DataPath() string {
	return s.dataPath
}

func (s *Store) RootPath() string {
	return s.rootPath
}
````

````go
// Package mount manages virtual filesystem mount points.
// It routes VFS operations to the correct underlying FileSystem based on path prefix.
package mount

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"path"
	"strings"
	"sync"

	"wails-app/vfs"
)

// Manager routes VFS operations to the correct FileSystem based on mount point.
// Mounts are resolved deepest-first so that /a/b/c takes priority over /a/b.
//
// Manager satisfies the vfs.Mounter interface.
type Manager struct {
	mu     sync.RWMutex
	mounts []entry // ordered deepest-first
	root   vfs.FileSystem
	nextID int
}

type entry struct {
	mountPoint string
	fs         vfs.FileSystem
	volume     vfs.Volume
	readOnly   bool
}

// NewManager creates a Manager with root as the "/" filesystem.
func NewManager(root vfs.FileSystem) *Manager {
	return &Manager{
		root:   root,
		mounts: make([]entry, 0),
	}
}

// Mount registers fs at mountPoint.
// Implements vfs.Mounter.
func (m *Manager) Mount(mountPoint string, fs vfs.FileSystem, readOnly bool, name string, vtype vfs.VolumeType) (vfs.Volume, error) {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()

	mountPoint = clean(mountPoint)

	for _, e := range m.mounts {
		if e.mountPoint == mountPoint {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("mount: %q is already mounted", mountPoint)
		}
	}

	vol := &volume{
		id:       fmt.Sprintf("vol-%d", m.nextID),
		name:     name,
		vtype:    vtype,
		root:     mountPoint,
		fs:       fs,
		mgr:      m,
		readOnly: readOnly,
	}
	m.nextID++

	e := entry{
		mountPoint: mountPoint,
		fs:         fs,
		volume:     vol,
		readOnly:   readOnly,
	}

	// Keep sorted by descending length (deepest first).
	inserted := false
	for i, existing := range m.mounts {
		if len(mountPoint) > len(existing.mountPoint) {
			m.mounts = append(m.mounts[:i], append([]entry{e}, m.mounts[i:]...)...)
			inserted = true
			break
		}
	}
	if !inserted {
		m.mounts = append(m.mounts, e)
	}

	return vol, nil
}

// Unmount removes the mount at mountPoint and closes the FS if it is an io.Closer.
// Implements vfs.Mounter.
func (m *Manager) Unmount(mountPoint string) error {
	m.mu.Lock()
	defer m.mu.Unlock()

	mountPoint = clean(mountPoint)

	for i, e := range m.mounts {
		if e.mountPoint == mountPoint {
			if closer, ok := e.fs.(io.Closer); ok {
				_ = closer.Close()
			}
			m.mounts = append(m.mounts[:i], m.mounts[i+1:]...)
			return nil
		}
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("mount: %q not found", mountPoint)
}

// Resolve finds the deepest mount covering path and returns its FileSystem,
// the path translated into that FS's namespace, and the Volume (nil = root FS).
// Implements vfs.Mounter.
func (m *Manager) Resolve(path string) (vfs.FileSystem, string, vfs.Volume, error) {
	m.mu.RLock()
	defer m.mu.RUnlock()

	path = clean(path)

	for _, e := range m.mounts {
		mp := e.mountPoint
		if path == mp || strings.HasPrefix(path, mp+"/") {
			rel := strings.TrimPrefix(path, mp)
			if rel == "" {
				rel = "/"
			}
			return e.fs, rel, e.volume, nil
		}
	}

	return m.root, path, nil, nil
}

// ListMounts returns a snapshot of all current mounts.
// Implements vfs.Mounter.
func (m *Manager) ListMounts() []vfs.MountedEntry {
	m.mu.RLock()
	defer m.mu.RUnlock()

	result := make([]vfs.MountedEntry, len(m.mounts))
	for i, e := range m.mounts {
		result[i] = vfs.MountedEntry{
			MountPoint: e.mountPoint,
			FS:         e.fs,
			Volume:     e.volume,
			ReadOnly:   e.readOnly,
		}
	}
	return result
}

// clean normalises a mount point to an absolute clean slash-separated path.
func clean(p string) string {
	if p == "" {
		return "/"
	}
	return path.Clean("/" + strings.TrimPrefix(p, "/"))
}

// volume implements vfs.Volume.
type volume struct {
	id       string
	name     string
	vtype    vfs.VolumeType
	root     string
	fs       vfs.FileSystem
	mgr      *Manager
	readOnly bool
}

func (v *volume) ID() string           { return v.id }
func (v *volume) Name() string         { return v.name }
func (v *volume) Type() vfs.VolumeType { return v.vtype }
func (v *volume) Root() string         { return v.root }
func (v *volume) IsReadOnly() bool     { return v.readOnly }
func (v *volume) Unmount() error       { return v.mgr.Unmount(v.root) }

var _ vfs.Volume = (*volume)(nil)
var _ vfs.Mounter = (*Manager)(nil)
````

````go
	RegistryKind() string
	RegistryValueType() string
	RegistryPreview() string
````

## File: vfs/registry/registry.go
````go
//go:build windows

// Package registry exposes the Windows Registry as a vfs.FileSystem.
//
// # Mapping
//
// The registry tree maps naturally onto the VFS directory model:
//
//	Registry concept          VFS concept
//	────────────────────────  ─────────────────────────────────────
//	Hive (HKLM, HKCU, …)     top-level directory
//	Key                       directory
//	Named value               file
//	Default value ("")        file named "(default)"
//
// ReadDir on a key returns both its subkeys (as dirs) and its values (as files)
// in a single listing, matching how a real file manager would show a key.
//
// # Value serialisation
//
// Values are serialised to UTF-8 text so they can be read through the File
// interface.  The format mirrors .reg file conventions:
//
//	REG_SZ / REG_EXPAND_SZ   the string, no decoration
//	REG_MULTI_SZ              one string per line
//	REG_DWORD / REG_QWORD     decimal (hex in parentheses): 4294967295 (0xFFFFFFFF)
//	REG_BINARY                upper-case hex pairs: DE AD BE EF …
//	REG_NONE / unknown        "(empty)" or hex dump
//
// # Write support
//
// Create/Mkdir/Remove/Rename delegate to the appropriate registry API calls.
// Most write operations require elevation; the OS returns access-denied
// naturally and the error is propagated as-is — no special handling needed.
//
// Rename is not supported by the registry API and always returns ErrReadOnly.
//
// # Build constraints
//
// This file only compiles on Windows.  A companion registry_stub.go provides
// a no-op New() for other platforms so the rest of the codebase compiles
// everywhere without build tags at the call site.
package registry

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"golang.org/x/sys/windows/registry"

	"wails-app/vfs"
)

// ── Hive table ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type hiveEntry struct {
	name string
	key  registry.Key
}

var hives = []hiveEntry{
	{"HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE", registry.LOCAL_MACHINE},
	{"HKEY_CURRENT_USER", registry.CURRENT_USER},
	{"HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT", registry.CLASSES_ROOT},
	{"HKEY_USERS", registry.USERS},
	{"HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG", registry.CURRENT_CONFIG},
	// Short aliases — resolved in openKey.
	{"HKLM", registry.LOCAL_MACHINE},
	{"HKCU", registry.CURRENT_USER},
	{"HKCR", registry.CLASSES_ROOT},
	{"HKU", registry.USERS},
	{"HKCC", registry.CURRENT_CONFIG},
}

// canonical returns the canonical long name for a hive abbreviation.
var canonical = map[string]string{
	"HKLM": "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE",
	"HKCU": "HKEY_CURRENT_USER",
	"HKCR": "HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT",
	"HKU":  "HKEY_USERS",
	"HKCC": "HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG",
}

// ── FS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// FS implements vfs.FileSystem over the Windows Registry.
type FS struct{}

// New returns an FS that exposes the Windows Registry.
// The returned error is always nil on Windows; the companion stub returns
// ErrNotSupported on other platforms.
func New() (*FS, error) {
	return &FS{}, nil
}

// ── path helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// splitPath breaks a VFS path into (hiveName, subkeyPath, valueName).
//
// Rules:
//   - path ""  or "/"        → root listing (no hive)
//   - path "HKLM"            → hive root, no subkey, no value
//   - path "HKLM/SOFTWARE"   → hive=HKLM, subkey="SOFTWARE", no value
//
// Whether the last component is a subkey or a value name is determined by
// actually opening it at call time (Stat/Open), not here.
func splitPath(path string) (hive, subkey string) {
	path = strings.Trim(strings.ReplaceAll(path, "\\", "/"), "/")
	if path == "" {
		return "", ""
	}
	parts := strings.SplitN(path, "/", 2)
	hive = strings.ToUpper(parts[0])
	if c, ok := canonical[hive]; ok {
		hive = c
	}
	if len(parts) == 2 {
		subkey = parts[1]
	}
	return hive, subkey
}

// rootKey returns the registry.Key constant for the named hive.
func rootKey(hiveName string) (registry.Key, bool) {
	upper := strings.ToUpper(hiveName)
	if c, ok := canonical[upper]; ok {
		upper = c
	}
	for _, h := range hives {
		if h.name == upper {
			return h.key, true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}

func isPermissionError(err error) bool {
	if err == nil {
		return false
	}
	if os.IsPermission(err) {
		return true
	}
	msg := strings.ToLower(err.Error())
	return strings.Contains(msg, "permission denied") ||
		strings.Contains(msg, "access is denied") ||
		strings.Contains(msg, "operation not permitted") ||
		strings.Contains(msg, "eacces") ||
		strings.Contains(msg, "eperm")
}

func mapLookupError(err error) error {
	if err == nil {
		return nil
	}
	if isPermissionError(err) {
		return fs.ErrPermission
	}
	return vfs.ErrNotFound
}

func mapAccessError(err error) error {
	if err == nil {
		return nil
	}
	if isPermissionError(err) {
		return fs.ErrPermission
	}
	return err
}

// openKey opens the registry key for path with the requested access mask.
// It returns the open key and the value name component (empty if path is a key).
// Caller must close the returned key when done (unless it is a hive root).
func openKey(path string, access uint32) (key registry.Key, valueName string, isHiveRoot bool, err error) {
	hiveName, subkey := splitPath(path)
	if hiveName == "" {
		return 0, "", false, vfs.ErrNotFound
	}

	root, ok := rootKey(hiveName)
	if !ok {
		return 0, "", false, vfs.ErrNotFound
	}

	if subkey == "" {
		// Path is the hive root itself — not a real openable key, but valid.
		return root, "", true, nil
	}

	// Try opening subkey directly first.
	k, err := registry.OpenKey(root, strings.ReplaceAll(subkey, "/", "\\"), access)
	if err == nil {
		return k, "", false, nil
	}
	if isPermissionError(err) {
		return 0, "", false, fs.ErrPermission
	}

	// If that failed, maybe the last component is a value name.
	idx := strings.LastIndex(subkey, "/")
	if idx < 0 {
		// e.g. "HKLM/SomeName" where SomeName is a value of the hive root.
		// Try treating the whole subkey as a value of the hive root.
		return root, subkey, true, nil
	}

	parentSubkey := subkey[:idx]
	valName := subkey[idx+1:]
	pk, err2 := registry.OpenKey(root, strings.ReplaceAll(parentSubkey, "/", "\\"), access)
	if err2 != nil {
		return 0, "", false, mapLookupError(err2)
	}
	return pk, valName, false, nil
}

// ── FileSystem interface ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

func (f *FS) Open(_ context.Context, path string) (vfs.File, error) {
	k, valName, isHiveRoot, err := openKey(path, registry.QUERY_VALUE)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !isHiveRoot {
		defer k.Close()
	}

	if valName == "" {
		// Path points to a key, not a value — not a readable file.
		return nil, vfs.ErrNotFile
	}

	value, err := readRegistryValue(k, valName)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	info := &valueInfo{
		path:      path,
		name:      valName,
		size:      int64(len(value.data)),
		modTime:   time.Time{},
		valueType: value.valueType,
		preview:   value.preview,
	}
	return &regFile{reader: bytes.NewReader(value.data), info: info}, nil
}

func (f *FS) Stat(_ context.Context, path string) (vfs.FileInfo, error) {
	path = strings.Trim(strings.ReplaceAll(path, "\\", "/"), "/")

	// Root.
	if path == "" {
		return &keyInfo{path: "", name: "registry", isRoot: true}, nil
	}

	hiveName, subkey := splitPath(path)
	if hiveName == "" {
		return nil, vfs.ErrNotFound
	}

	// Hive root.
	if subkey == "" {
		root, ok := rootKey(hiveName)
		if !ok {
			return nil, vfs.ErrNotFound
		}
		_ = root
		return &keyInfo{path: path, name: hiveName}, nil
	}

	root, ok := rootKey(hiveName)
	if !ok {
		return nil, vfs.ErrNotFound
	}

	// Try as a key.
	k, err := registry.OpenKey(root, strings.ReplaceAll(subkey, "/", "\\"), registry.QUERY_VALUE)
	if err == nil {
		defer k.Close()
		return &keyInfo{path: path, name: lastName(path)}, nil
	}
	if isPermissionError(err) {
		return nil, fs.ErrPermission
	}

	// Try as a value.
	idx := strings.LastIndex(subkey, "/")
	var parentKey registry.Key
	var valName string
	if idx < 0 {
		parentKey = root
		valName = subkey
	} else {
		pk, err2 := registry.OpenKey(root, strings.ReplaceAll(subkey[:idx], "/", "\\"), registry.QUERY_VALUE)
		if err2 != nil {
			return nil, mapLookupError(err2)
		}
		defer pk.Close()
		parentKey = pk
		valName = subkey[idx+1:]
	}

	value, err := readRegistryValue(parentKey, valName)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, mapLookupError(err)
	}
	return &valueInfo{
		path:      path,
		name:      valName,
		size:      int64(len(value.data)),
		valueType: value.valueType,
		preview:   value.preview,
	}, nil
}

func (f *FS) ReadDir(_ context.Context, path string) ([]vfs.FileInfo, error) {
	path = strings.Trim(strings.ReplaceAll(path, "\\", "/"), "/")

	// Root — list hives.
	if path == "" {
		result := make([]vfs.FileInfo, 0, 5)
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		for _, h := range hives {
			if seen[h.name] || len(h.name) <= 4 { // skip short aliases
				continue
			}
			seen[h.name] = true
			result = append(result, &keyInfo{path: h.name, name: h.name})
		}
		return result, nil
	}

	hiveName, subkey := splitPath(path)
	root, ok := rootKey(hiveName)
	if !ok {
		return nil, vfs.ErrNotFound
	}

	var k registry.Key
	if subkey == "" {
		k = root
	} else {
		var err error
		k, err = registry.OpenKey(root, strings.ReplaceAll(subkey, "/", "\\"),
			registry.ENUMERATE_SUB_KEYS|registry.QUERY_VALUE)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, mapLookupError(err)
		}
		defer k.Close()
	}

	var result []vfs.FileInfo

	// Subkeys → directories.
	subkeyNames, err := k.ReadSubKeyNames(-1)
	if err == nil {
		for _, name := range subkeyNames {
			childPath := path + "/" + name
			result = append(result, &keyInfo{path: childPath, name: name})
		}
	} else if isPermissionError(err) {
		return nil, fs.ErrPermission
	}

	// Values → files.
	valueNames, err := k.ReadValueNames(-1)
	if err == nil {
		for _, name := range valueNames {
			displayName := name
			if name == "" {
				displayName = "(default)"
			}
			value, _ := readRegistryValue(k, name)
			childPath := path + "/" + displayName
			result = append(result, &valueInfo{
				path:      childPath,
				name:      displayName,
				size:      int64(len(value.data)),
				valueType: value.valueType,
				preview:   value.preview,
			})
		}
	} else if isPermissionError(err) {
		return nil, fs.ErrPermission
	}

	return result, nil
}

func (f *FS) Exists(ctx context.Context, path string) bool {
	info, err := f.Stat(ctx, path)
	return err == nil && info != nil
}

// ── Write operations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Create creates a new REG_SZ value at path.  The caller writes the string
// value through the returned File; on Close the value is written.
func (f *FS) Create(_ context.Context, path string) (vfs.File, error) {
	k, valName, _, err := openKey(path, registry.SET_VALUE)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if valName == "" {
		k.Close()
		return nil, vfs.ErrNotFile
	}
	return &writeFile{key: k, valName: valName}, nil
}

// Mkdir creates a new registry key at path.
func (f *FS) Mkdir(_ context.Context, path string, _ fs.FileMode) error {
	hiveName, subkey := splitPath(path)
	root, ok := rootKey(hiveName)
	if !ok {
		return vfs.ErrNotFound
	}
	if subkey == "" {
		return vfs.ErrExists
	}
	k, _, err := registry.CreateKey(root, strings.ReplaceAll(subkey, "/", "\\"), registry.SET_VALUE)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("registry mkdir %q: %w", path, mapAccessError(err))
	}
	k.Close()
	return nil
}

// Remove deletes a registry key or value at path.
func (f *FS) Remove(_ context.Context, path string) error {
	hiveName, subkey := splitPath(path)
	root, ok := rootKey(hiveName)
	if !ok {
		return vfs.ErrNotFound
	}
	if subkey == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("registry remove: cannot delete hive root")
	}

	// Try as a key first.
	err := registry.DeleteKey(root, strings.ReplaceAll(subkey, "/", "\\"))
	if err == nil {
		return nil
	}

	// Try as a value.
	idx := strings.LastIndex(subkey, "/")
	var parentKey registry.Key
	var valName string
	if idx < 0 {
		parentKey = root
		valName = subkey
	} else {
		pk, err2 := registry.OpenKey(root, strings.ReplaceAll(subkey[:idx], "/", "\\"), registry.SET_VALUE)
		if err2 != nil {
			return mapLookupError(err2)
		}
		defer pk.Close()
		parentKey = pk
		valName = subkey[idx+1:]
	}
	if err2 := parentKey.DeleteValue(valName); err2 != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("registry remove value %q: %w", valName, mapAccessError(err2))
	}
	return nil
}

// Rename is not supported by the registry API.
func (f *FS) Rename(_ context.Context, _, _ string) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("registry: rename not supported")
}

// ── Path helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

func (f *FS) Join(elem ...string) string        { return strings.Join(elem, "/") }
func (f *FS) IsAbs(path string) bool            { return false } // registry paths are always relative to root
func (f *FS) RealPath(_ string) (string, error) { return "", nil }

func (f *FS) Split(path string) (string, string) {
	i := strings.LastIndex(path, "/")
	if i < 0 {
		return "", path
	}
	return path[:i], path[i+1:]
}

// ── Value serialisation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type registryValueData struct {
	data      []byte
	valueType string
	preview   string
}

// readRegistryValue reads a registry value and serialises it to UTF-8 bytes.
func readRegistryValue(k registry.Key, name string) (registryValueData, error) {
	// Try as string (REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ).
	if s, valueType, err := k.GetStringValue(name); err == nil {
		return registryValueData{
			data:      []byte(s),
			valueType: registryTypeName(valueType),
			preview:   previewRegistryValue(s),
		}, nil
	}

	// Try as integer (REG_DWORD, REG_QWORD).
	if n, valueType, err := k.GetIntegerValue(name); err == nil {
		serialized := fmt.Sprintf("%d (0x%X)", n, n)
		return registryValueData{
			data:      []byte(serialized),
			valueType: registryTypeName(valueType),
			preview:   serialized,
		}, nil
	}

	// Try as multi-string (REG_MULTI_SZ).
	if ss, valueType, err := k.GetStringsValue(name); err == nil {
		serialized := strings.Join(ss, "\n")
		return registryValueData{
			data:      []byte(serialized),
			valueType: registryTypeName(valueType),
			preview:   previewRegistryValue(serialized),
		}, nil
	}

	// Fall back to binary (REG_BINARY, REG_NONE, unknown).
	b, valueType, err := k.GetBinaryValue(name)
	if err != nil {
		return registryValueData{}, fmt.Errorf("registry: read value %q: %w", name, err)
	}
	serialized := "(empty)"
	if len(b) == 0 {
		return registryValueData{
			data:      []byte(serialized),
			valueType: registryTypeName(valueType),
			preview:   serialized,
		}, nil
	}
	var sb strings.Builder
	for i, byt := range b {
		if i > 0 {
			sb.WriteByte(' ')
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%02X", byt)
	}
	serialized = sb.String()
	return registryValueData{
		data:      []byte(serialized),
		valueType: registryTypeName(valueType),
		preview:   previewRegistryValue(serialized),
	}, nil
}

func registryTypeName(valueType uint32) string {
	switch valueType {
	case registry.NONE:
		return "REG_NONE"
	case registry.SZ:
		return "REG_SZ"
	case registry.EXPAND_SZ:
		return "REG_EXPAND_SZ"
	case registry.BINARY:
		return "REG_BINARY"
	case registry.DWORD:
		return "REG_DWORD"
	case registry.DWORD_BIG_ENDIAN:
		return "REG_DWORD_BIG_ENDIAN"
	case registry.LINK:
		return "REG_LINK"
	case registry.MULTI_SZ:
		return "REG_MULTI_SZ"
	case registry.RESOURCE_LIST:
		return "REG_RESOURCE_LIST"
	case registry.FULL_RESOURCE_DESCRIPTOR:
		return "REG_FULL_RESOURCE_DESCRIPTOR"
	case registry.RESOURCE_REQUIREMENTS_LIST:
		return "REG_RESOURCE_REQUIREMENTS_LIST"
	case registry.QWORD:
		return "REG_QWORD"
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("REG_0x%X", valueType)
	}
}

func previewRegistryValue(value string) string {
	preview := strings.ReplaceAll(value, "\r\n", " | ")
	preview = strings.ReplaceAll(preview, "\n", " | ")
	preview = strings.ReplaceAll(preview, "\t", " ")
	preview = strings.TrimSpace(preview)
	if preview == "" {
		return "(empty)"
	}
	const limit = 120
	if len(preview) > limit {
		return preview[:limit-1] + "..."
	}
	return preview
}

func lastName(path string) string {
	i := strings.LastIndex(path, "/")
	if i < 0 {
		return path
	}
	return path[i+1:]
}

// ── keyInfo ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type keyInfo struct {
	path   string
	name   string
	isRoot bool
}

func (k *keyInfo) Name() string       { return k.name }
func (k *keyInfo) Size() int64        { return 0 }
func (k *keyInfo) Mode() fs.FileMode  { return fs.ModeDir | 0555 }
func (k *keyInfo) ModTime() time.Time { return time.Time{} }
func (k *keyInfo) IsDir() bool        { return true }
func (k *keyInfo) Sys() any           { return nil }

func (k *keyInfo) Path() string         { return k.path }
func (k *keyInfo) RealPath() string     { return "" }
func (k *keyInfo) Volume() vfs.Volume   { return nil }
func (k *keyInfo) IsArchive() bool      { return false }
func (k *keyInfo) IsHidden() bool       { return false }
func (k *keyInfo) IsSymlink() bool      { return false }
func (k *keyInfo) IsNested() bool       { return false }
func (k *keyInfo) MountChain() []string { return nil }
func (k *keyInfo) RegistryKind() string { return "Key" }
func (k *keyInfo) RegistryValueType() string {
	return ""
}
func (k *keyInfo) RegistryPreview() string { return "" }

// ── valueInfo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type valueInfo struct {
	path      string
	name      string
	size      int64
	modTime   time.Time
	valueType string
	preview   string
}

func (v *valueInfo) Name() string       { return v.name }
func (v *valueInfo) Size() int64        { return v.size }
func (v *valueInfo) Mode() fs.FileMode  { return 0444 }
func (v *valueInfo) ModTime() time.Time { return v.modTime }
func (v *valueInfo) IsDir() bool        { return false }
func (v *valueInfo) Sys() any           { return nil }

func (v *valueInfo) Path() string         { return v.path }
func (v *valueInfo) RealPath() string     { return "" }
func (v *valueInfo) Volume() vfs.Volume   { return nil }
func (v *valueInfo) IsArchive() bool      { return false }
func (v *valueInfo) IsHidden() bool       { return false }
func (v *valueInfo) IsSymlink() bool      { return false }
func (v *valueInfo) IsNested() bool       { return false }
func (v *valueInfo) MountChain() []string { return nil }
func (v *valueInfo) RegistryKind() string { return "Value" }
func (v *valueInfo) RegistryValueType() string {
	return v.valueType
}
func (v *valueInfo) RegistryPreview() string { return v.preview }

// ── regFile (read) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

type regFile struct {
	reader *bytes.Reader
	info   *valueInfo
}

func (f *regFile) Read(p []byte) (int, error)  { return f.reader.Read(p) }
func (f *regFile) Write(_ []byte) (int, error) { return 0, vfs.ErrReadOnly }
func (f *regFile) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error) {
	return f.reader.Seek(offset, whence)
}
func (f *regFile) Close() error                { return nil }
func (f *regFile) Stat() (vfs.FileInfo, error) { return f.info, nil }
func (f *regFile) Sync() error                 { return nil }

// ── writeFile (write) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// writeFile buffers written bytes and commits them as REG_SZ on Close.
type writeFile struct {
	key     registry.Key
	valName string
	buf     bytes.Buffer
}

func (w *writeFile) Read(_ []byte) (int, error) { return 0, io.EOF }
func (w *writeFile) Seek(_ int64, _ int) (int64, error) {
	return 0, fmt.Errorf("registry write file: seek not supported")
}
func (w *writeFile) Write(p []byte) (int, error) { return w.buf.Write(p) }
func (w *writeFile) Sync() error                 { return nil }
func (w *writeFile) Stat() (vfs.FileInfo, error) {
	return &valueInfo{name: w.valName, size: int64(w.buf.Len())}, nil
}
func (w *writeFile) Close() error {
	defer w.key.Close()
	return w.key.SetStringValue(w.valName, w.buf.String())
}

// Compile-time interface check.
var _ vfs.FileSystem = (*FS)(nil)
````

````go
package smb

import "testing"

func TestCleanUsesShareRelativePaths(t *testing.T) {
	fs := &FS{}

	tests := []struct {
		name string
		in   string
		want string
	}{
		{name: "empty root", in: "", want: "."},
		{name: "dot root", in: ".", want: "."},
		{name: "slash root", in: "/", want: "."},
		{name: "nested path", in: "/oleks/Downloads/unlocker", want: "oleks/Downloads/unlocker"},
		{name: "backslashes", in: `\oleks\Downloads\unlocker`, want: "oleks/Downloads/unlocker"},
	}

	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := fs.clean(tc.in); got != tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("clean(%q) = %q, want %q", tc.in, got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
````

````go
package vfs

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
)

// Sentinel errors
var (
	ErrReadOnly = errors.New("filesystem is read-only")
	ErrNotFound = errors.New("path not found")
	ErrNotDir   = errors.New("path is not a directory")
	ErrNotFile  = errors.New("path is not a file")
	ErrExists   = errors.New("path already exists")
)

// FileInfo extends fs.FileInfo with VFS-specific metadata.
type FileInfo interface {
	fs.FileInfo
	Path() string     // Full VFS path
	RealPath() string // Underlying real path (if applicable)
	Volume() Volume   // Source volume (nil for nested archive entries)
	IsArchive() bool  // True if the entry can be mounted as a sub-filesystem
	IsHidden() bool
	IsSymlink() bool
	IsNested() bool       // Lives inside an archive chain
	MountChain() []string // Archive chain leading here
}

// Volume represents a mounted filesystem.
type Volume interface {
	ID() string
	Name() string
	Type() VolumeType
	Root() string
	IsReadOnly() bool
	Unmount() error
}

type VolumeType string

const (
	VolumeLocal    VolumeType = "local"
	VolumeArchive  VolumeType = "archive"
	VolumeRemote   VolumeType = "remote"
	VolumeMemory   VolumeType = "memory"
	VolumeRegistry VolumeType = "registry"
)

// FileSystem is the core VFS interface every adapter must implement.
// Write operations return ErrReadOnly on read-only filesystems rather than panicking.
type FileSystem interface {
	// Read operations
	Open(ctx context.Context, path string) (File, error)
	Stat(ctx context.Context, path string) (FileInfo, error)
	ReadDir(ctx context.Context, path string) ([]FileInfo, error)
	Exists(ctx context.Context, path string) bool

	// Write operations — may return ErrReadOnly
	Create(ctx context.Context, path string) (File, error)
	Mkdir(ctx context.Context, path string, perm fs.FileMode) error
	Remove(ctx context.Context, path string) error
	Rename(ctx context.Context, oldPath, newPath string) error

	// Path helpers
	Join(elem ...string) string
	Split(path string) (dir, file string)
	IsAbs(path string) bool

	// RealPath translates a VFS path to the underlying OS path, if applicable.
	// Returns ("", nil) for purely virtual filesystems (in-memory archives, etc.).
	RealPath(vfsPath string) (string, error)
}

// File represents an open file handle inside the VFS.
type File interface {
	io.Reader
	io.Writer
	io.Seeker
	io.Closer
	Stat() (FileInfo, error)
	Sync() error
}
````

````go
package main

import (
	internalcontracts "wails-app/internal/contracts"
	internalops "wails-app/internal/ops"
)

// ============================================================================
// Typed Error Codes
// ============================================================================

// AppErrorCode is a stable machine-readable string sent with every
// BatchItemError so the frontend can show localised / actionable messages.
type AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.AppErrorCode

type BatchItemError = internalcontracts.BatchItemError

const (
	ErrCodePermissionDenied AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.ErrCodePermissionDenied
	ErrCodeNotFound         AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.ErrCodeNotFound
	ErrCodeDiskFull         AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.ErrCodeDiskFull
	ErrCodeReadOnly         AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.ErrCodeReadOnly
	ErrCodeAlreadyExists    AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.ErrCodeAlreadyExists
	ErrCodeInvalidPath      AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.ErrCodeInvalidPath
	ErrCodeCancelled        AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.ErrCodeCancelled
	ErrCodeUnknown          AppErrorCode = internalcontracts.ErrCodeUnknown
)

// ============================================================================
// OS Info
// ============================================================================

type OSType = internalcontracts.OSType

const (
	OSWindows OSType = internalcontracts.OSWindows
	OSLinux   OSType = internalcontracts.OSLinux
	OSDarwin  OSType = internalcontracts.OSDarwin
	OSUnknown OSType = internalcontracts.OSUnknown
)

type OSInfoResponse = internalcontracts.OSInfoResponse

// ============================================================================
// Drives

type SchemeType = internalcontracts.SchemeType

const (
	SchemeFixed     SchemeType = internalcontracts.SchemeFixed
	SchemeRemovable SchemeType = internalcontracts.SchemeRemovable
````

````markdown
# Declarative directory plugin example

`plugin.json` contains package identity, permissions and activation policy.
`frontend.json` is a data-only contribution document. The directory loader does not import or evaluate JavaScript from plugin folders.

A declarative command delegates to an already registered host/backend command through `targetCommandId`. Toolbar and context-menu entries then place that plugin-owned command in the UI.
````

## File: docs/BROWSER_PANE_BRIDGE.md
````markdown
# Browser Pane Bridge

## Purpose

`internal/browserpane` hosts a native child webview for a surface and exposes a uniform bidirectional message bridge to Angular and to the page loaded inside that child webview.

The bridge is used for two separate concerns:

- Application messages between Angular and the child page.
- Internal browser-pane messages such as resource snapshots used by the web resource cache.

This document describes the runtime contract, the message flow, and the platform-specific delivery behavior.

## Architecture

The bridge is a relay, not a direct Angular-to-page JavaScript call.

Host to child flow:

`Angular -> Wails binding -> Go browser pane service -> native webview -> child page`

Child to host flow:

`child page -> native webview message handler -> Go browser pane service -> Wails event -> Angular`

The common bridge logic lives in:

- `internal/browserpane/message_bridge.go`
- `internal/browserpane/service.go`
- `frontend/src/app/services/native-browser-pane.service.ts`

Platform adapters live in:

- `internal/browserpane/pane_windows.go`
- `internal/browserpane/pane_linux.go`
- `internal/browserpane/pane_darwin.go`

## Shared Page API

Every platform injects the same bootstrap script into the child page before or during document load. That script installs `window.__wailsBrowserPane`.

The injected bridge provides:

- `window.__wailsBrowserPane.postMessage(payload)`
- `window.__wailsBrowserPane.receiveHostMessage(raw)`
- `window.__wailsBrowserPane.onmessage`
- `window.__wailsBrowserPane.parseMessage(raw)`

It also dispatches a DOM event when the host posts a message into the page:

- `wails-browser-pane-message`

Message serialization rules:

- The native boundary always carries a string.
- Objects are serialized with `JSON.stringify(...)`.
- `undefined` is normalized to the string `"null"`.
- On receipt, the bridge tries `JSON.parse(...)`.
- If parsing fails, the raw string is delivered unchanged.

## Host To Child

Angular sends a message with `NativeBrowserPaneService.postMessage(surfaceId, message)`.

Runtime path:

1. `NativeBrowserPaneService.postMessage(...)` serializes the payload to a string and calls `window.go.app.App.BrowserPanePostMessage(surfaceId, message)`.
2. `App.BrowserPanePostMessage(...)` forwards to `browserpane.Service.PostMessage(...)`.
3. `browserpane.Service` resolves the pane by `surfaceId` and calls the platform pane's `PostMessage(...)`.
4. The platform layer evaluates the shared host-delivery script returned by `browserPaneHostMessageEvalScript(...)`.
5. Inside the child page, the injected bridge dispatches the `wails-browser-pane-message` event and also invokes `window.__wailsBrowserPane.onmessage(...)` when a handler is set.

Angular entry points:

- `frontend/src/app/services/native-browser-pane.service.ts`
- `internal/app/bindings_browserpane.go`
- `internal/browserpane/service.go`

Page-side receive options:

```js
window.addEventListener('wails-browser-pane-message', (event) => {
  console.log('host event detail', event.detail);
});

window.__wailsBrowserPane.onmessage = ({ data, rawData }) => {
  console.log('host message', data, rawData);
};
```

## Child To Host

The child page sends a message with `window.__wailsBrowserPane.postMessage(payload)`.

Runtime path:

1. The injected bridge serializes the payload to a string.
2. The bridge sends that string through the native webview message channel.
3. The platform adapter receives the native message and forwards it into Go.
4. `handleBrowserPaneBridgeMessage(...)` inspects the payload.
5. Internal bridge messages are consumed by Go.
6. All other messages are emitted back to Angular as the Wails event `browser-pane:message`.

Angular subscribes through:

- `NativeBrowserPaneService.onMessage(...)`
- `NativeBrowserPaneService.onSurfaceMessage(surfaceId, ...)`

Angular receives:

- `surfaceId`: assigned by the host, not by the child page
- `message`: the raw string payload
- `data`: parsed JSON when valid, otherwise the raw string

Page-side send example:

```js
window.__wailsBrowserPane?.postMessage({
  type: 'child-ready',
  title: document.title,
  href: location.href,
});
```

Angular-side receive example:

```ts
const stop = nativeBrowserPane.onSurfaceMessage(surfaceId, ({ message, data }) => {
  console.log('raw', message);
  console.log('parsed', data);
});
```

## Reserved Internal Messages

The bridge reserves one message type for host-managed behavior:

- `type: "resource-snapshot"`

When Go receives that message type, it does not forward it as a normal app message. Instead it:

- Normalizes `pageUrl`
- Stores the resource list in `webresourcecache`
- Emits `web:resourcesChanged` when the cache changed

Application code should not reuse `type: "resource-snapshot"` unless it intentionally wants to target this internal cache path.

## Page Ready And Queueing

Host-to-child delivery is queued until the current page is ready to execute injected JavaScript.

Platform behavior:

- Windows queues host messages until WebView2 navigation completes.
- Linux queues scripts until WebKit reports `WEBKIT_LOAD_FINISHED`.
- macOS queues scripts until `WKWebView` reports `didFinishNavigation`.

This means:

- Calling `BrowserPanePostMessage(...)` immediately after navigation is valid.
- The message is not dropped just because the page is still loading.
- Delivery order is preserved within a pane.

Child-to-host messages are only available after the bootstrap script is present in the page.

## Platform Transport

The page uses the native transport available on the active platform.

- Windows: `window.chrome.webview.postMessage(...)`
- Linux WebKitGTK: `window.webkit.messageHandlers.wailsBrowserPane.postMessage(...)`
- macOS WKWebView: `window.webkit.messageHandlers.wailsBrowserPane.postMessage(...)`

The Go side normalizes these platform differences into the same callback path.

## Practical Contract

For application messages, treat the bridge as a JSON-over-string channel with host-assigned `surfaceId`.

Recommended conventions:

- Send JSON objects with an explicit `type`.
- Keep payloads self-contained and serializable.
- Avoid overloading reserved internal message types.
- Subscribe per surface when the same Angular session can host multiple child panes.

Recommended message shape:

```json
{
  "type": "example",
  "payload": {
    "id": "123"
  }
}
```

## Current Limitations

- The bridge is message-based only. There is no request-response correlation, timeout handling, or RPC layer on top of it.
- The native boundary carries strings, so large payloads should be avoided unless there is a clear reason.
- Internal `resource-snapshot` traffic shares the same transport as app messages, even though Go treats it specially.

If the bridge grows beyond simple event-style traffic, the next step should be an explicit protocol layer with:

- message IDs
- request and response types
- versioning
- error envelopes
- optional backpressure limits
````

## File: docs/INPUT_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md
````markdown
# Input System Architecture

## Objective

Replace the current mix of global shortcuts and component-local key handlers with a unified input system that supports:

- VS Code-style keybinding resolution
- Chord shortcuts such as `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`
- Mouse gestures
- Plugin-provided bindings
- Dynamic rebinding at runtime
- Context priority resolution

The immediate goal of this document is to define the dialog and overlay binding surface so the refactor starts from a complete inventory instead of ad hoc handlers.

## Current State

The frontend input model has completed its core migration. The architecture now consists of:

- `frontend/src/app/services/input-engine.service.ts` — the primary engine with context-aware resolution, command registration, source-priority binding resolution, plugin binding registration, and pending chord state.
- `frontend/src/app/services/dialog-input-catalog.ts` — canonical binding catalog for all dialogs and overlays.
- Component-level command registration via `InputEngineService` for dialogs, overlays, and widgets.
- `frontend/src/app/services/keyboard.service.ts` — now acts as a compatibility adapter that registers legacy global shortcuts into the shared engine instead of dispatching through a separate listener.
- `frontend/src/app/services/shortcut-registry.service.ts` — still defines the default global shortcut set, but those bindings now resolve through the shared engine with DOM-aware `when` guards and per-binding propagation control.

A small number of local `HostListener` or template `keydown` handlers remain as fallback behavior in a few surfaces, but the canonical path for all new bindings is command-first.

## Dialog And Overlay Inventory

### Dialogs / Modals

All dialogs below now register commands via `InputEngineService` and acquire their input context via `InputContextService`. Bindings are defined in `frontend/src/app/services/dialog-input-catalog.ts`.

| Surface | Context ID | Bindings |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm dialog | `dialog.confirm` | `Enter` (accept), `Escape` (cancel), `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` (focus), `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` (focus) |
| Archive move warning | `dialog.archiveMoveWarning` | `Enter` (confirm), `Escape` (cancel), `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` (focus), `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` (focus) |
| Global search | `dialog.globalSearch` | `Escape` (close), `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (navigate), `Enter` (open), `Ctrl+Enter` (open folder), `Ctrl+,` (settings) |
| Global search settings | `dialog.globalSearch.settings` | `Escape` (close), `Enter` (apply), `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` (focus) |
| Keyboard help | `dialog.keyboardHelp` | `Escape` (close), `Ctrl+F` (focus search), `Ctrl+S` (export), `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (navigate), `Space` (toggle) |
| Path history viewer | `dialog.pathHistory` | `Escape` (close), `Ctrl+F` (focus filter), `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (navigate), `Enter` (open), `Delete` (remove), `Ctrl+Delete` (clear all) |
| Filter custom dialog | `filter-bar.component.ts` | `Escape` closes via parent listener; inline filter widget handles its own keys |

### Overlays

All overlays below now have dedicated input contexts and command bindings.

| Surface | Context ID | Bindings |
|---|---|---|
| Address bar quick access | `overlay.quickAccess` | `Escape` (close), `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` (section), `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (item), `Enter` (open), `Delete` (remove pin) |
| Address bar edit | `overlay.addressBar.edit` | `Enter`, `Escape`, `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`, arrows |
| Drive dropdown | `overlay.addressBar.schemes` | `Escape` (close), `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (item), `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` (column), `Enter` (open) |
| Sibling dropdown | `overlay.addressBar.siblings` | `Escape` (close), `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (item), `Enter` (open) |
| Workspace selector menu | `overlay.workspaceSelector` | `Escape` (close), `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (item), `Enter` (activate), `Delete` (delete) |
| Filter preset/category dropdowns | `overlay.filter.presets` | `Escape` (close), `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` (item), `Enter` (select) |
| Filter widget | `widget.filterInline` | `Escape` (close), `Enter` / `F3` (next match), `Shift+Enter` / `Shift+F3` (prev match) |

## Target Architecture

### 1. Commands, Not Inline Closures

Bindings should target command IDs rather than component closures.

Examples:

- `dialog.confirm.accept`
- `dialog.confirm.cancel`
- `dialog.globalSearch.nextResult`
- `dialog.globalSearch.openSelected`
- `overlay.quickAccess.nextItem`
- `overlay.workspaceSelector.close`

Components can still implement the behavior, but command registration and binding registration must be separate concerns.

### 2. Resolver Model

The input engine should resolve events using this order:

1. Active modal/dialog context
2. Active overlay context
3. Focused widget context
4. Active pane context
5. Global context

Within the same context level, choose the highest priority binding by:

1. Context specificity
2. Source priority: user > workspace > plugin > default
3. Explicit numeric priority
4. Most recent registration as a final deterministic tie-breaker

### 3. Context Stack

The engine should maintain a stack of input contexts rather than infer everything from DOM traversal.

Each context should define:

- `id`
- `kind`: `global`, `pane`, `dialog`, `overlay`, `widget`
- `priority`
- optional parent context
- activation predicate or lifecycle hook

This is required for nested surfaces such as:

- Global search -> settings dialog
- Keyboard help -> import file flow -> confirm alert
- Pane -> address bar -> quick access overlay

### 4. Multi-Step Sequences

The engine must support keybinding sequences, not only single combinations.

Examples:

- `Ctrl+K Ctrl+C`
- `Ctrl+K Ctrl+S`
- `G G`

Sequence handling requirements:

- timeout window per chord sequence
- prefix matching
- cancellation on unmatched continuation
- visible pending-chord state so the UI can hint when the engine is waiting for the second step

### 5. Mouse Gestures

Mouse bindings should be first-class entries, not ad hoc pointer handlers.

Initial gesture families:

- click variants: left, middle, right, double-click
- wheel with modifiers
- drag gestures with button and modifier state
- path gestures such as right-drag menu triggers

Examples:

- `mouse.doubleClick.left` -> `pane.openSelection`
- `mouse.drag.right` -> `pane.showDragOperationMenu`
- `mouse.wheel.ctrl` -> `viewer.zoom`

### 6. Dynamic Rebinding

Bindings must be editable at runtime and reloaded without restarting the app.

Required layers:

- built-in defaults
- plugin defaults
- workspace overrides
- user overrides

The current import/export behavior in `keyboard.service.ts` can become one persistence layer, but the runtime engine should treat it as data rather than direct mutable state on shortcut objects.

### 7. Plugin Bindings

Plugins should be able to contribute:

- commands
- contexts
- keybindings
- mouse gestures

Plugin bindings must declare:

- stable source ID
- binding source type `plugin`
- optional when/context expression
- optional weight/priority

## Canonical Dialog Binding Matrix

This matrix defines the initial target command surface for every dialog-like UI.

### Confirm Dialog

Context ID: `dialog.confirm`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Enter` | `dialog.confirm.accept` |
| `Escape` | `dialog.confirm.cancel` |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | `dialog.confirm.focusNext` / `dialog.confirm.focusPrev` |

### Archive Move Warning

Context ID: `dialog.archiveMoveWarning`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Enter` | `dialog.archiveMoveWarning.confirm` |
| `Escape` | `dialog.archiveMoveWarning.cancel` |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | `dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusNext` / `dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusPrev` |

### Global Search

Context ID: `dialog.globalSearch`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `dialog.globalSearch.close` |
| `ArrowUp` | `dialog.globalSearch.prevResult` |
| `ArrowDown` | `dialog.globalSearch.nextResult` |
| `Enter` | `dialog.globalSearch.openSelected` |
| `Ctrl+,` | `dialog.globalSearch.openSettings` |

Nested context ID: `dialog.globalSearch.settings`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `dialog.globalSearch.settings.close` |
| `Enter` | `dialog.globalSearch.settings.apply` |

### Keyboard Help

Context ID: `dialog.keyboardHelp`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `dialog.keyboardHelp.close` |
| `Ctrl+F` | `dialog.keyboardHelp.focusSearch` |
| `ArrowUp` | `dialog.keyboardHelp.prevItem` |
| `ArrowDown` | `dialog.keyboardHelp.nextItem` |
| `Space` | `dialog.keyboardHelp.toggleSelectedBinding` |
| `Ctrl+S` | `dialog.keyboardHelp.exportBindings` |

### Path History Viewer

Context ID: `dialog.pathHistory`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `dialog.pathHistory.close` |
| `Ctrl+F` | `dialog.pathHistory.focusFilter` |
| `ArrowUp` | `dialog.pathHistory.prevItem` |
| `ArrowDown` | `dialog.pathHistory.nextItem` |
| `Enter` | `dialog.pathHistory.openSelected` |
| `Delete` | `dialog.pathHistory.removeSelected` |
| `Ctrl+Delete` | `dialog.pathHistory.clearAll` |

### Filter Widget

Context ID: `widget.filterInline`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `widget.filterInline.close` |
| `Enter` | `widget.filterInline.nextMatch` |
| `Shift+Enter` | `widget.filterInline.prevMatch` |
| `F3` | `widget.filterInline.nextMatch` |
| `Shift+F3` | `widget.filterInline.prevMatch` |

### Address Bar Quick Access

Context ID: `overlay.quickAccess`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `overlay.quickAccess.close` |
| `Tab` | `overlay.quickAccess.nextSection` |
| `Shift+Tab` | `overlay.quickAccess.prevSection` |
| `ArrowUp` | `overlay.quickAccess.prevItem` |
| `ArrowDown` | `overlay.quickAccess.nextItem` |
| `Enter` | `overlay.quickAccess.openSelected` |
| `Delete` | `overlay.quickAccess.removePinnedSelected` |

### Address Bar Drive Dropdown

Context ID: `overlay.addressBar.drives`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `overlay.addressBar.drives.close` |
| `ArrowUp` | `overlay.addressBar.drives.prevItem` |
| `ArrowDown` | `overlay.addressBar.drives.nextItem` |
| `Enter` | `overlay.addressBar.drives.openSelected` |

### Address Bar Sibling Dropdown

Context ID: `overlay.addressBar.siblings`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `overlay.addressBar.siblings.close` |
| `ArrowUp` | `overlay.addressBar.siblings.prevItem` |
| `ArrowDown` | `overlay.addressBar.siblings.nextItem` |
| `Enter` | `overlay.addressBar.siblings.openSelected` |

### Workspace Selector

Context ID: `overlay.workspaceSelector`

| Binding | Command |
|---|---|
| `Escape` | `overlay.workspaceSelector.close` |
| `ArrowUp` | `overlay.workspaceSelector.prevItem` |
| `ArrowDown` | `overlay.workspaceSelector.nextItem` |
| `Enter` | `overlay.workspaceSelector.activateSelected` |
| `Delete` | `overlay.workspaceSelector.deleteSelected` |

## Migration Plan

### Phase A ✅ Complete

- Introduced typed input-system model and dialog binding catalog.
- Bridged existing keyboard shortcut registrations through the new engine.
- Catalog is the read-only source of truth for design and audit.

### Phase B ✅ Complete

- `keyboard.service.ts` now acts as a compatibility adapter registering into the shared engine.
- Dialog key handlers moved from local `HostListener` logic into command bindings.
- Resolver supports contexts, source priority, and chords.

### Phase C 🔄 In Progress

- Mouse gesture dispatch exists in the input engine for click, double-click, button, and wheel gestures.
- Browser-shell mouse bindings cover file-entry double-click open and viewer `Ctrl+Wheel` zoom.
- Plugin contribution API surface is designed but not yet wired end-to-end.
- UI for live rebinding and conflict inspection is not yet implemented.

## Start Point For This Refactor

All dialog and overlay contexts listed above are live. Further work should focus on:

1. Expanding mouse gesture coverage as more commands are migrated.
2. Implementing the live-rebinding UI.
3. Completing the plugin binding contribution API.

## Implementation Status

All core input system features are implemented:

- `frontend/src/app/services/input-engine.service.ts` — context registration, command registration, source-priority binding resolution, plugin binding registration, pending chord state, and mouse gesture dispatch.
- `frontend/src/app/services/dialog-input-catalog.ts` — canonical binding catalog for all dialogs and overlays.
- `frontend/src/app/services/input-context.service.ts` — lease-counted context activation.

Dialog contexts:
- `dialog.confirm`
- `dialog.archiveMoveWarning`
- `dialog.globalSearch`
- `dialog.globalSearch.settings`
- `dialog.keyboardHelp`
- `dialog.pathHistory`

Overlay contexts:
- `overlay.quickAccess`
- `overlay.addressBar.schemes`
- `overlay.addressBar.siblings`
- `overlay.workspaceSelector`
- `overlay.filter.presets`

Widget contexts:
- `widget.filterInline`
- `overlay.addressBar.edit`

Legacy adapter:
- `keyboard.service.ts` registers legacy shortcuts into the shared engine.
- `shortcut-registry.service.ts` bindings resolve through the shared engine with DOM-aware `when` guards.

Remaining work (Phase C):
- Plugin binding contribution API end-to-end wiring.
- Live-rebinding UI.
- Expanded mouse gesture coverage as more commands migrate.
````

## File: docs/PLUGIN_DIRECTORY_MODULE.md
````markdown
# Declarative directory plugin module v1

Directory packages may include an optional `frontend.json` beside `plugin.json`.
The host reads and validates this file as data. It does **not** import or evaluate JavaScript from the plugin directory.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "commands": [
    {
      "id": "refresh",
      "title": "Refresh",
      "name": "refresh",
      "targetCommandId": "pane.nav.refresh"
    }
  ],
  "toolbar": [
    { "id": "refresh", "commandId": "refresh", "when": "always" }
  ],
  "contextMenu": [
    { "id": "refresh", "commandId": "refresh", "when": "selection" }
  ]
}
```

`targetCommandId` must reference an existing host/backend command. The directory loader creates a plugin-owned command descriptor that delegates to that target and inherits its enabled state.

Placement `when` values in schema v1 are `always`, `selection`, and `single-selection`.

This loader intentionally cannot execute arbitrary frontend code, start processes, load DLLs, or load WASM. Those require a separate sandboxed executable-plugin design.
````

## File: docs/REFACTOR_ROADMAP.md
````markdown
# Refactor Roadmap

## Purpose

This roadmap turns the current refactor effort into a staged plan with clear boundaries, target files, and acceptance criteria. The goal is to keep behavior stable while reducing the size and coupling of the largest orchestration files in both the Go backend and Angular frontend.

## Working Rules

- Preserve current user-visible behavior unless a phase explicitly says otherwise.
- Keep archive behavior, pane behavior, and view-operation parity intact during each split.
- Prefer extraction behind existing interfaces over broad rewrites.
- Validate each phase with `npm run build` and `go build .` unless the phase is docs-only.
- Do not combine large frontend and backend behavioral changes in the same phase.

## Phase 1: Finish Frontend Pane Decomposition

Status: Complete

### Objective

Shrink [frontend/src/app/components/file-pane.component.ts](frontend/src/app/components/file-pane.component.ts) into a host/facade and move the remaining mixed filesystem/archive action flows into smaller controllers.

### Target Files

- [frontend/src/app/components/file-pane.component.ts](frontend/src/app/components/file-pane.component.ts)
- [frontend/src/app/components/file-browser.component.ts](frontend/src/app/components/file-browser.component.ts)

- New: `frontend/src/app/components/file-pane-preview.controller.ts` if quick view and frozen preview logic remains coupled

### Scope

- Extract delete, rename, copy-to-other, move-to-other, drag-drop, and destination-path logic into an operations controller.
- Extract preview tab opening and archive-aware viewer-tab bootstrapping if it still mixes with pane navigation.
- Leave template ownership in `file-pane.component.ts`; move only orchestration logic.

### Acceptance Criteria

- `file-pane.component.ts` acts mainly as a host and event adapter.
- Archive operations and filesystem operations are separated behind explicit host interfaces.
- Copy, move, delete, rename, quick preview, and drag-drop behavior remain unchanged in list, grid, details, and tree views.
- No new direct cross-controller coupling is added inside the component.
- `npm run build` passes.

## Phase 2: Stabilize Frontend Surface Boundaries

Status: Complete

### Objective

Make the dynamic surface system easier to reason about by reducing implicit state sharing between pane, surface runtime, and viewer host layers.

### Target Files

### Scope

- Clarify which state belongs to the pane, which belongs to a dir session, and which belongs to a rendered surface.
- Remove redundant surface re-resolution triggers.
- Reduce best-effort imperative calls from pane to child components where a VM contract can carry the same intent.

- Surface re-rendering occurs only on meaningful context changes.
- Directory surface runtime responsibilities are documented in code by interface shape, not only by naming.
- Viewer host and dir surface host use the same stability rules for dynamic rendering.
- No blank-screen or partial-render regressions in `wails dev`.
- `npm run build` passes.

## Phase Order

1. Finish frontend pane decomposition.
2. Stabilize frontend surface boundaries.
3. Split backend archive domain internals.
4. Extract app-level backend services.
5. Consolidate shared contracts and documentation.

## Phase Exit Checklist

Use this checklist at the end of each non-doc phase.

- Target files are smaller and have clearer ownership than before.
- Public behavior in file operations, tab behavior, archive behavior, and preview behavior is unchanged.
- No new circular dependencies or host/controller leaks were introduced.
- `npm run build` passes.
- `go build .` passes.
- Any architecture notes changed by the phase are updated in this roadmap or linked docs.
````

````markdown
# Keyboard Shortcuts & Mouse Handlers

## Architecture Notes

Keyboard and mouse interactions now route through the refactored pane/surface boundaries rather than directly through one large component.

The next-stage input-system design, including dialog-by-dialog binding inventory and requirements for chords, plugin bindings, mouse gestures, dynamic rebinding, and context-priority resolution, is documented in [INPUT_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md](INPUT_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md).

Current migration status:

- dialog contexts now run through the new input engine for confirm, global search, keyboard help, path history, and archive move warning surfaces
- overlay contexts now run through the new input engine for address-bar quick access, drive and sibling dropdowns, the workspace selector, and filter dropdown overlays
- legacy global shortcuts are now bridged through the new input engine by `keyboard.service.ts` and still sourced from `shortcut-registry.service.ts`
- global chord shortcuts are now live through the same bridge, with pending-chord feedback surfaced in the browser chrome
- mouse gesture dispatch is now live in `input-engine.service.ts` for click, double-click, button, and wheel bindings
- the first browser-shell mouse bindings now route through that engine as well: file-entry double-click opens the active selection, and viewer `Ctrl+Wheel` zooms the active preview

- Global keyboard dispatch starts in the frontend keyboard services and browser shell components.
- Pane-facing browser actions are grouped through pane command factories instead of many standalone pane methods.
- `file-pane.component.ts` acts mainly as a host/facade; deeper interaction logic belongs in pane controllers, view controllers, or surface VMs.
- When adding a shortcut or pointer interaction, preserve behavior parity across list, grid, details, and tree views.

#### Search Scheme Input

The address bar accepts direct `search://` expressions in edit mode.

Supported forms:

- `search://invoice @ C:/Work`
- `search://invoice @@ C:/Work`
- `search://invoice`
- `search://?path=filesystem://c/Work&pattern=invoice&recursive=true`

Rules:

- `@` means recursive search.
- `@@` means non-recursive search.
- If no path is supplied, the current pane location is used.
- Enter normalizes these expressions to the canonical search alias consumed by the backend.

|----------|---------|-------------|
| **Arrow Up/Down** | Tree View | Navigate up/down nodes |
| **Arrow Left** | Tree View | Collapse current node or go to parent |
| **Arrow Right** | Tree View | Expand current node or go to first child |
| **Home** | Tree View | Go to first node |
| **End** | Tree View | Go to last visible node |
| **Enter** | Tree View | Navigate into selected directory |
| **Space** | Tree View | Toggle selection |
| **F2** | Tree View | Rename node |
| **Ctrl+A** | Tree View | Select all nodes |

### Modal & Dialog Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Context | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| **Escape** | Modal/Dialog | Close active modal, dialog, or dropdown |
| **Arrow Up/Down** | Dropdown/List | Navigate list items |
| **Enter** | Dropdown/List | Select current item |
| **?** | Global | Show keyboard help (same as Ctrl+/) |

## Implementation Notes

### Global Keyboard Service
- **File:** [keyboard.service.ts](frontend/src/app/services/keyboard.service.ts)
- Acts as a compatibility adapter over the shared input engine rather than owning a separate global keyboard listener
- Registers legacy shortcut definitions as engine bindings on the `global` context
- Preserves legacy context rules (`global`, `pane`, `filter`, `modal`) through DOM-aware `when` guards
- Preserves `allowBubble` behavior by controlling per-binding propagation in the engine

### Shortcut Registry
- **File:** [shortcut-registry.service.ts](frontend/src/app/services/shortcut-registry.service.ts)
- Registers all default keyboard shortcuts during app initialization
- Organized by category: navigation, tabs, files, search, workspace, pane
- Connects keyboard events to callback functions in main component

### Tab Completion System
- **Location:** Address Bar Edit Mode
- Idle-slash pipeline: After 1 second of typing idle, auto-appends `/` and loads directory children
- **Tab:** Cycle forward through suggestions, restart idle timer
- **Shift+Tab:** Cycle backward through suggestions or go up to parent
- Typing any key clears tab session and returns to normal mode
- Search expressions are parsed on commit rather than treated as filesystem paths

### Mouse Selection Modes
1. **Single Click:** Select item (Ctrl for multi-select, Shift for range)
2. **Double Click:** Open/navigate into item
3. **Middle Click:** Alternative action (e.g., close tab)
4. **Right Click:** Show context menu
5. **Drag:** Start rubber-band selection or initiate drag-and-drop
6. **Click + Drag:** Rubber-band multi-select in file views

### Drag and Drop Flow
1. **Drag Start:** Collect selected entries, set drag data, emit dragStart event
2. **Drag Over:** Determine drop target and position, show visual feedback
3. **Drag Leave:** Clear drop indicators
4. **Drop:** Process drop with source entries and target, execute move/copy operation
5. **Drag End:** Clean up drag state

### Context Menu System
- Right-click on files/folders shows operations menu (copy, cut, delete, rename, etc.)
- Right-click on empty space shows background menu (paste, new folder, etc.)
- Right-click on address bar breadcrumbs shows segment menu (navigate to, copy path, pin, open in other pane)
- Context menus support Escape key to close

### Event Propagation Control
- Most interactive elements use `event.stopPropagation()` to prevent bubbling
- Drop-down/modal backdrop handlers stop propagation to keep menu open when clicking inside
- Tab completion needs `allowBubble: true` to reach component handlers while still preventing default browser behavior

---

### Total Commander Compatibility
The application implements Total Commander function key shortcuts:
- **F3:** Quick view
- **F5:** Copy to other pane
- **F6:** Move to other pane
- **F7:** New folder
- **F8:** Delete
- **Shift+F6:** Rename

### Windows Explorer Compatibility
- **Alt+D:** Focus address bar
- **Backspace:** Go to parent directory

### Modern Application Shortcuts

- **Ctrl+Tab:** Tab switching
````

## File: docs/SUPPORTED_FILES_BY_VIEWER.md
````markdown
# Viewer Support - Selected Formats

## Font Viewer

Font files are previewed directly in-app with a dedicated font surface. The viewer renders sample text, multilingual glyph rows, and basic file metadata.

Supported detection:
- By extension: TTF, TTC, OTF, OTC, WOFF, WOFF2, EOT
- By MIME: font/* plus common legacy font MIME types

This also covers extensionless web-font cache files when the backend probe resolves them as font MIME types.

## Image Viewer

## Browser-Native Formats
These formats are rendered directly by the browser without conversion:
- PNG (including Apple CgBI)
- JPEG
- GIF
- SVG
- WebP
- BMP
- ICO
- AVIF
- TIFF

## Convertible Formats (with Backend Processing)
The following formats are converted to PNG for preview via libvips. **libvips must be installed** for extended format support; without it, only basic formats can be used.

### With libvips Installed:
- JPEG 2000 (JP2, J2K)
- OpenEXR (EXR)
- HEIF/HEIC (Apple High Efficiency)
- AVIF
- TIFF
- WebP
- JPEG XL (JXL)
- FITS / HDR / PFM
- Exact coverage still depends on how the bundled libvips build was compiled

### Without libvips (Go Fallback):
- PNG
- JPEG
- GIF
- BMP

## Architecture

The image viewer uses a two-tier approach:

1. **Tier 1 (Native):** Browser directly renders supported formats
2. **Tier 2 (Conversion):** For unsupported formats, backend converts to PNG via libvips

Converted previews are not sent through the Wails bridge as base64 payloads. They are served from the local preview stream as regular image URLs, which keeps transport overhead lower and lets the browser load them normally.

See [IMAGE_CONVERTER_PIPELINE.md](IMAGE_CONVERTER_PIPELINE.md) for detailed architecture and setup instructions.

## Installation

To enable full format support, install libvips:

**Windows:**
```powershell
choco install vips
# or download a Windows build from https://www.libvips.org/
```

**macOS:**
```bash
brew install vips
```

**Linux:**
```bash
sudo apt-get install libvips-tools
```

## Format Categories

### Original Supported
PNG (including Apple CgBI), JPEG, GIF, SVG, TIFF, ICO, BMP, WebP, AVIF, HEIF/HEIC, JPEG 2000, OpenEXR, JPEG XL, FITS, HDR, PFM, and browser-native formats.

### Notes
- Archive images (inside ZIP, RAR, etc.) cannot be converted yet
- Very large images may take time to convert on first load
- Converted images are served from the local preview stream as regular image URLs
````

````typescript
 *   - Entries ARE extracted to the destination (tracked in operation toast)
 *   - Source entries ARE deleted from the archive (archive is rewritten)
 *   - For nested archives: extraction runs, deletion is skipped

 *   <app-archive-move-warning
 *     [visible]="archiveMoveWarning"
 *     [entryCount]="archivePendingMoveEntries.length"

export class ArchiveMoveWarningComponent implements OnInit, OnChanges, OnDestroy {
  @ViewChild('dialogPanel') private dialogPanel?: ElementRef<HTMLElement>;

  private releaseDialogContext: (() => void) | null = null;

  @Input()  visible    = false;
  @Input()  entryCount = 1;
  @Output() confirmed  = new EventEmitter<void>();
  @Output() cancelled  = new EventEmitter<void>();

  constructor(
    private inputContexts: InputContextService,
    private inputEngine: InputEngineService,
  ) {}

  ngOnInit(): void {
    this.inputEngine.registerCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.confirm', () => {
      if (!this.visible) return;
      this.confirmed.emit();
    });

    this.inputEngine.registerCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.cancel', () => {
      if (!this.visible) return;
      this.cancelled.emit();
    });

    this.inputEngine.registerCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusNext', () => {
      if (!this.visible) return;
      this.moveDialogFocus(1);
    });

    this.inputEngine.registerCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusPrev', () => {
      if (!this.visible) return;
      this.moveDialogFocus(-1);
    });

    this.inputEngine.registerCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusNextArrow', () => {
      if (!this.visible || !this.shouldUseActionArrowNavigation()) return;
      this.moveActionFocus(1);
    });

    this.inputEngine.registerCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusPrevArrow', () => {
      if (!this.visible || !this.shouldUseActionArrowNavigation()) return;
      this.moveActionFocus(-1);
    });

    this.syncContextLease();
  }

  ngOnChanges(_changes: SimpleChanges): void {
    this.syncContextLease();
  }

  ngOnDestroy(): void {
    this.releaseDialogContext?.();
    this.releaseDialogContext = null;
    this.inputEngine.unregisterCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.confirm');
    this.inputEngine.unregisterCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.cancel');
    this.inputEngine.unregisterCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusNext');
    this.inputEngine.unregisterCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusPrev');
    this.inputEngine.unregisterCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusNextArrow');
    this.inputEngine.unregisterCommand('dialog.archiveMoveWarning.focusPrevArrow');
  }

  onBackdrop(e: MouseEvent): void {
    if ((e.target as HTMLElement).classList.contains('amw-backdrop')) {
      this.cancelled.emit();
    }
  }

  private syncContextLease(): void {
    if (this.visible) {
      this.releaseDialogContext ??= this.inputContexts.acquire('dialog.archiveMoveWarning');
      return;
    }

    this.releaseDialogContext?.();
    this.releaseDialogContext = null;
  }

  private moveDialogFocus(delta: number): void {
    const panel = this.dialogPanel?.nativeElement;
    if (!panel) {
      return;
    }

    moveFocusWithin(panel, delta);
  }

  private moveActionFocus(delta: number): void {
    const panel = this.dialogPanel?.nativeElement;
    if (!panel) {
      return;
    }

    moveFocusWithin(panel, delta, '[data-dialog-action]');
  }

  private shouldUseActionArrowNavigation(): boolean {
    const panel = this.dialogPanel?.nativeElement;
    const activeElement = document.activeElement;
    if (!panel || !(activeElement instanceof HTMLElement) || !panel.contains(activeElement)) {
      return false;
    }

    return !!activeElement.closest('[data-dialog-action]');
  }
}
````

````typescript
import { CommonModule } from '@angular/common';
import { Component, ElementRef, ViewChild } from '@angular/core';
import { FormsModule } from '@angular/forms';
import { createSubject, takeUntil, type Stream } from '@epikodelabs/streamix';
import { DialogFocusTrapDirective } from '../directives/dialog-focus-trap.directive';

import { NativeOverlayFreezeService } from '../services/native-overlay-freeze.service';
import {
  BatchRenameDialogService,
  type BatchRenameItem,
  type BatchRenameRequest,
} from '../services/batch-rename-dialog.service';

function splitNameExt(name: string): { stem: string; ext: string } {
  if (name.startsWith('.')) {
    const dot = name.indexOf('.', 1);
    if (dot === -1) return { stem: name, ext: '' };
    return { stem: name.slice(0, dot), ext: name.slice(dot) };
  }
  const dot = name.lastIndexOf('.');
  if (dot === -1) return { stem: name, ext: '' };
  return { stem: name.slice(0, dot), ext: name.slice(dot) };
}

function applyPattern(
  name: string,
  pattern: string,
  counter: number,
  counterWidth: number
): string {
  const { stem, ext } = splitNameExt(name);
  let result = '';
  let i = 0;
  while (i < pattern.length) {
    const ch = pattern[i];
    if (ch === '*') {
      result += stem;
      i++;
    } else if (ch === '&') {
      result += ext;
      i++;
    } else if (ch === '#') {
      let width = 0;
      while (i + width < pattern.length && pattern[i + width] === '#') {
        width++;
      }
      const pad = Math.max(width, counterWidth);
      result += String(counter).padStart(pad, '0');
      i += width;
    } else {
      result += ch;
      i++;
    }
  }
  return result;
}

interface PreviewRow {
  entry: BatchRenameItem['entry'];
  newName: string;
  conflict: boolean;
}

@Component({
  selector: 'app-batch-rename-dialog',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [CommonModule, FormsModule, DialogFocusTrapDirective],
  styleUrls: ['./batch-rename-dialog.component.scss'],
  template: `
    <ng-container *ngIf="request$ | async as request">
      <div class="br-overlay" (click)="onCancel()">
        <div
          #dialogPanel
          class="br-panel"
          [appTrapFocus]="true"
          role="dialog"
          aria-modal="true"
          aria-label="Batch Rename"
          tabindex="-1"
          (click)="$event.stopPropagation()"
        >
          <header class="br-header">
            <h2>Batch Rename</h2>
            <span class="br-subtitle">{{ request.items.length }} item(s) selected</span>
          </header>

          <div class="br-body">
            <div class="br-controls">
              <div class="br-field">
                <label for="br-pattern">Pattern</label>
                <input
                  id="br-pattern"
                  class="br-input"
                  type="text"
                  [(ngModel)]="pattern"
                  (input)="onPatternChange()"
                  placeholder="e.g. photo_###&"
                  data-dialog-initial-focus
                />
                <div class="br-hint">
                  <code>*</code> = original name, <code>&amp;</code> = extension,
                  <code>#</code> = counter (## pads to 2 digits)
                </div>
              </div>

              <div class="br-row">
                <div class="br-field br-field--small">
                  <label for="br-start">Start at</label>
                  <input
                    id="br-start"
                    class="br-input"
                    type="number"
                    min="0"
                    [(ngModel)]="startAt"
                    (input)="onPatternChange()"
                  />
                </div>
                <div class="br-field br-field--small">
                  <label for="br-step">Step</label>
                  <input
                    id="br-step"

                    min="1"
                    [(ngModel)]="increment"

                  />

              <div class="br-preview-header">
                <span>Preview</span>
                <span *ngIf="conflictCount > 0" class="br-conflict-badge">
                  {{ conflictCount }} conflict(s)
                </span>
              </div>
              <div class="br-preview-list">
                <div
                  *ngFor="let row of preview"
                  class="br-preview-row"
                  [class.br-preview-row--conflict]="row.conflict"

                  <span class="br-preview-old" [title]="row.entry.name">{{ row.entry.name }}</span>
                  <span class="br-preview-arrow">

                    </svg>
                  </span>
                  <span class="br-preview-new" [title]="row.newName">{{ row.newName }}</span>
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <footer class="br-footer">
            <button
              type="button"
              class="br-btn br-btn--secondary"
              (click)="onCancel()"
            >
              Cancel
            </button>
            <button
              type="button"
              class="br-btn br-btn--primary"
              [disabled]="conflictCount > 0 || preview.length === 0"
              (click)="onApply()"

              Rename

    </ng-container>

export class BatchRenameDialogComponent {
  @ViewChild('dialogPanel') dialogPanel?: ElementRef<HTMLElement>;

  readonly request$: Stream<BatchRenameRequest | null> = this.service.activeRequest$;

  pattern = '*';
  startAt = 1;
  increment = 1;
  preview: PreviewRow[] = [];
  conflictCount = 0;

  private readonly destroy$ = createSubject<void>();

  constructor(
    private readonly service: BatchRenameDialogService,
    private readonly freeze: NativeOverlayFreezeService,
  ) {
    this.service.activeRequest$.pipe(takeUntil(this.destroy$)).subscribe((req) => {
      if (req) {
        this.pattern = '*';
        this.startAt = 1;
        this.increment = 1;
        this.rebuildPreview(req);
        this.freeze.acquire('batch-rename-dialog');
      } else {
        this.freeze.release('batch-rename-dialog');
      }
    });
  }

  onPatternChange(): void {
    const req = this.service.activeRequest$.value;
    if (req) {
      this.rebuildPreview(req);
    }
  }

  private rebuildPreview(req: BatchRenameRequest): void {
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    const rows: PreviewRow[] = [];
    let counter = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(this.startAt) || 0));
    const step = Math.max(1, Math.floor(Number(this.increment) || 1));

    // Determine counter width from pattern
    let counterWidth = 1;
    const pat = this.pattern;
    for (let i = 0; i < pat.length; i++) {
      if (pat[i] === '#') {
        let w = 1;
        while (i + w < pat.length && pat[i + w] === '#') w++;
        counterWidth = Math.max(counterWidth, w);
      }
    }

    for (const item of req.items) {
      const newName = applyPattern(item.entry.name, pat, counter, counterWidth);
      const conflict = seen.has(newName) || newName === '';
      seen.add(newName);
      rows.push({ entry: item.entry, newName, conflict });
      counter += step;
    }

    this.preview = rows;
    this.conflictCount = rows.filter((r) => r.conflict).length;
  }

  onCancel(): void {
    this.service.resolveActive(null);
  }

  onApply(): void {
    const req = this.service.activeRequest$.value;
    if (!req || this.conflictCount > 0) return;

    const result: BatchRenameItem[] = this.preview.map((row) => ({
      entry: row.entry,
      newName: row.newName,
    }));
    this.service.resolveActive(result);
  }
}
````
